6f9ca4b7-157d-56c9-9302-e7ad08c615c0.title: Solving an Initial Value Problem Involving a Cauchy-Euler Equation with a Repeated Root

e-6627.knowledge_point: Solving a Cauchy-Euler Equation with a Repeated Root
e-6627.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
2x^2 y'' + 6 xy' + 2y = 0, \qquad x>0.
$$
e-6627.worked_solution:
This is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume the solutions take the form $y=x^\lambda.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
y' = \lambda x^{\lambda -1}, \qquad y'' = \lambda(\lambda-1)x^{\lambda-2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}+6x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+2{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ 2\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }+6\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+2{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[2\lambda (\lambda -1)+6\lambda +2] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following characteristic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\lambda (\lambda -1)+6\lambda +2 & =0 \\ 2{\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +2 & =0 \\ 2({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +1) & =0 \\ 2(\lambda +1)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The characteristic equation has a double root $\lambda = -1.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(x) & ={c}_{1}{x}^{-1}+{c}_{2}{x}^{-1}\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =\frac{{c}_{1}}{x}+\frac{{c}_{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-6628.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem Involving a Cauchy-Euler Equation with a Repeated Root
e-6628.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
x^2 y'' - 19 xy' + 100y = 0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y =c_1 x^{10}+ c_2x ^{10}\ln x ,
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
x^2 y'' - 19 xy' + 100y = 0, \quad y(1) = 0,\quad  y'(1)=1, \quad x>0.
$$
e-6628.worked_solution:
We find the constants $c_1$ and $c_2$ using the initial conditions.

- First, we apply the condition $y(1)=0.$ Substituting $y(1)= 0$ into the general solution gives

$$
0= c_1.
$$

- Then, we apply the condition $y'(1) = 1.$ Differentiating $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =10{c}_{1}{x}^{9}+{c}_{2}{x}^{9}+10{c}_{2}{x}^{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $y'(1)=1$ and $c_1 = 0$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =10{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\ 1 & =0+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(x) = x ^{10}\ln x .
$$

y(t)=c1t5+c2t5ln⁡t
b
y(t)=c1t+c2t3ln⁡t

decision.explanation: Substituting y=t^r gives 2r(r-1)+22r+50=2(r+5)^2=0. The repeated root r=-5 yields y(t)=c₁t⁻⁵+c₂t⁻⁵ ln t for t>0, so option e is correct.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
2{t}^{2}{y}^{″}+22t{y}^{′}+50y=0,\,t>0.
$$
after.worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={t}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {t}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}+22t\cdot \lambda {t}^{\lambda -1}+50{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ 2\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }+22\lambda {t}^{\lambda }+50{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[2\lambda (\lambda -1)+22\lambda +50] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2\lambda (\lambda -1)+22\lambda +50 & =0 \\ 2{\lambda }^{2}+20\lambda +50 & =0 \\ 2({\lambda }^{2}+10\lambda +25) & =0 \\ 2(\lambda +5)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =-5.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(t)={c}_{1}{t}^{-5}+{c}_{2}{t}^{-5}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.
$$

after.html:
Question 1
?

Find the general solution to the equation 2t2y″+22ty′+50y=0,t>0.

a
y(t)=c1t5+c2t5ln⁡t
b
y(t)=c1t+c2t3ln⁡t
c
y(t)=c1t3+c2t3ln⁡t
d
y(t)=c1t5+c2t−5
e
y(t)=c1t−5+c2t−5ln⁡t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form y=tλ. Differentiating y with respect to t gives

y′=λtλ−1,y″=λ(λ−1)tλ−2.

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

2t2⋅λ(λ−1)tλ−2+22t⋅λtλ−1+50tλ=02λ(λ−1)tλ+22λtλ+50tλ=0tλ[2λ(λ−1)+22λ+50]=0.

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

2λ(λ−1)+22λ+50=02λ2+20λ+50=02(λ2+10λ+25)=02(λ+5)2=0.

Hence, we have a double root λ=−5. Therefore, the general solution is y(t)=c1t−5+c2t−5ln⁡t.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Cauchy-Euler Equation with a Repeated Root
content.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
2{t}^{2}{y}^{″}+22t{y}^{′}+50y=0,\,t>0.
$$
content.worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={t}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {t}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}+22t\cdot \lambda {t}^{\lambda -1}+50{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ 2\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }+22\lambda {t}^{\lambda }+50{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[2\lambda (\lambda -1)+22\lambda +50] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2\lambda (\lambda -1)+22\lambda +50 & =0 \\ 2{\lambda }^{2}+20\lambda +50 & =0 \\ 2({\lambda }^{2}+10\lambda +25) & =0 \\ 2(\lambda +5)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =-5.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(t)={c}_{1}{t}^{-5}+{c}_{2}{t}^{-5}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.
$$

Question 2
?

Find the general solution to the equation t2y″+13ty′+36y=0,t>0.

a
y(t)=c1t3+c2t−3
b
y(t)=c1t6+c2t6ln⁡t
c
y(t)=c1t−6+c2t−6ln⁡t
d
y(t)=c1t−6+c2ln⁡t
e
y(t)=c1t3+c2t3ln⁡t
Submit

decision.explanation: For y=t^r, the characteristic equation is r(r-1)+13r+36=r²+12r+36=(r+6)²=0. The repeated root r=-6 gives the general solution y(t)=c₁t⁻⁶+c₂t⁻⁶ ln t for t>0, matching option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}+13t{y}^{′}+36y=0,\,t>0.
$$
after.worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={t}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {t}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}+13t\cdot \lambda {t}^{\lambda -1}+36{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }+13\lambda {t}^{\lambda }+36{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)+13\lambda +36] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)+13\lambda +36 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+12\lambda +36 & =0 \\ (\lambda +6)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =-6.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(t)={c}_{1}{t}^{-6}+{c}_{2}{t}^{-6}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.
$$

Find the general solution to the equation t2y″+13ty′+36y=0,t>0.

a
y(t)=c1t3+c2t−3
b
y(t)=c1t6+c2t6ln⁡t
c

Submit

EXPLANATION

The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form y=tλ. Differentiating y with respect to t gives

y′=λtλ−1,y″=λ(λ−1)tλ−2.

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

t2⋅λ(λ−1)tλ−2+13t⋅λtλ−1+36tλ=0λ(λ−1)tλ+13λtλ+36tλ=0tλ[λ(λ−1)+13λ+36]=0.

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

λ(λ−1)+13λ+36=0λ2+12λ+36=0(λ+6)2=0.

Hence, we have a double root λ=−6. Therefore, the general solution is y(t)=c1t−6+c2t−6ln⁡t.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Cauchy-Euler Equation with a Repeated Root
content.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}+13t{y}^{′}+36y=0,\,t>0.
$$
content.worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={t}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {t}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}+13t\cdot \lambda {t}^{\lambda -1}+36{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }+13\lambda {t}^{\lambda }+36{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)+13\lambda +36] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)+13\lambda +36 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+12\lambda +36 & =0 \\ (\lambda +6)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =-6.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(t)={c}_{1}{t}^{-6}+{c}_{2}{t}^{-6}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.
$$

Question 3

Find the general solution to the equation x2y″−xy′+y=0,x>0.

a
 y(x)=c1x+c2x−1
b
 y(x)=c1x−2+c2x−2ln⁡x
c
 y(x)=c1x−1+c2
d
 y(x)=c1x+c2xln⁡x
e
 y(x)=c1x+c2x2
Submit

decision.explanation: Substituting y=x^r gives r(r-1)-r+1=(r-1)^2=0. The repeated root r=1 yields the general solution y(x)=c₁x+c₂x ln x for x>0, matching option d.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-x{y}^{′}+y=0,\,x>0.
$$
after.worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={x}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {x}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}-x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }-\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)-\lambda +1] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)-\lambda +1 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +1 & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =1.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(x)={c}_{1}{x}^{1}+{c}_{2}{x}^{1}\operatorname{ln}⁡x={c}_{1}x+{c}_{2}x\operatorname{ln}⁡x.
$$

Question 3
?

Find the general solution to the equation x2y″−xy′+y=0,x>0.

a
 y(x)=c1x+c2x−1
b
 y(x)=c1x−2+c2x−2ln⁡x
c
 y(x)=c1x−1+c2
d
 y(x)=c1x+c2xln⁡x
e
 y(x)=c1x+c2x2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form y=xλ. Differentiating y with respect to x gives

y′=λxλ−1,y″=λ(λ−1)xλ−2.

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Cauchy-Euler Equation with a Repeated Root
content.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-x{y}^{′}+y=0,\,x>0.
$$
content.worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={x}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {x}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}-x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }-\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)-\lambda +1] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)-\lambda +1 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +1 & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =1.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(x)={c}_{1}{x}^{1}+{c}_{2}{x}^{1}\operatorname{ln}⁡x={c}_{1}x+{c}_{2}x\operatorname{ln}⁡x.
$$

decision.explanation: Substituting y=x^r gives r(r-1)+19r+81=r²+18r+81=(r+9)²=0. The repeated root r=-9 yields y(x)=c₁x⁻⁹+c₂x⁻⁹ ln x for x>0, matching option c.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+19x{y}^{′}+81y=0,\,x>0.
$$
after.worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={x}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {x}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}+19x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+81{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }+19\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+81{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)+19\lambda +81] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)+19\lambda +81 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+18\lambda +81 & =0 \\ (\lambda +9)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =-9.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(x)={c}_{1}{x}^{-9}+{c}_{2}{x}^{-9}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.
$$

Question 4
?

Find the general solution to the equation x2y″+19xy′+81y=0,x>0.

a
y(x)=c1+c2x9ln⁡x
b
y(x)=c1x3+c2x3ln⁡x
c
y(x)=c1x−9+c2x−9ln⁡x
d
y(x)=c1x−3+c2x−3ln⁡x
e
y(x)=c1x9+c2x−9
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form y=xλ. Differentiating y with respect to x gives

y′=λxλ−1,y″=λ(λ−1)xλ−2.

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

x2⋅λ(λ−1)xλ−2+19x⋅λxλ−1+81xλ=0λ(λ−1)xλ+19λxλ+81xλ=0xλ[λ(λ−1)+19λ+81]=0.

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

λ(λ−1)+19λ+81=0λ2+18λ+81=0(λ+9)2=0.

Hence, we have a double root λ=−9. Therefore, the general solution is y(x)=c1x−9+c2x−9ln⁡x.

verification.explanation: The characteristic equation is r(r-1)+19r+81=(r+9)^2=0. The repeated root r=-9 gives y(x)=c₁x⁻⁹+c₂x⁻⁹ ln x, confirming option c and the revealed solution. The deliberately incorrect submission selected option d.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Cauchy-Euler Equation with a Repeated Root
content.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+19x{y}^{′}+81y=0,\,x>0.
$$
content.worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={x}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {x}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}+19x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+81{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }+19\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+81{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)+19\lambda +81] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)+19\lambda +81 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+18\lambda +81 & =0 \\ (\lambda +9)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =-9.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(x)={c}_{1}{x}^{-9}+{c}_{2}{x}^{-9}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.
$$

Question 5
?

Find the general solution to the equation 2t2y″+10ty′+8y=0,t>0.

a
y(t)=c1t−2+c2t2
b
y(t)=c1t−2+c2t−2ln⁡t
c
 y(t)=c1t−1+c2t−1ln⁡t
d
 y(t)=c1t+c2tln⁡t
e
y(t)=c1t+c2t2ln⁡t
Submit

decision.explanation: Substituting y=t^r gives 2r(r-1)+10r+8=2(r+2)^2=0. The repeated root r=-2 yields y(t)=c₁t⁻²+c₂t⁻² ln t for t>0, matching option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
2{t}^{2}{y}^{″}+10t{y}^{′}+8y=0,\,t>0.
$$
after.worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={t}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {t}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}+10t\cdot \lambda {t}^{\lambda -1}+8{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ 2\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }+10\lambda {t}^{\lambda }+8{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[2\lambda (\lambda -1)+10\lambda +8] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2\lambda (\lambda -1)+10\lambda +8 & =0 \\ 2{\lambda }^{2}+8\lambda +8 & =0 \\ 2({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +4) & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =-2.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(t)={c}_{1}{t}^{-2}+{c}_{2}{t}^{-2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.
$$

after.html:
Question 5
?

Find the general solution to the equation 2t2y″+10ty′+8y=0,t>0.

a
y(t)=c1t−2+c2t2
b
y(t)=c1t−2+c2t−2ln⁡t
c
 y(t)=c1t−1+c2t−1ln⁡t
d
 y(t)=c1t+c2tln⁡t
e
y(t)=c1t+c2t2ln⁡t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form y=tλ. Differentiating y with respect to t gives

y′=λtλ−1,y″=λ(λ−1)tλ−2.

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

2t2⋅λ(λ−1)tλ−2+10t⋅λtλ−1+8tλ=02λ(λ−1)tλ+10λtλ+8tλ=0tλ[2λ(λ−1)+10λ+8]=0.

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

2λ(λ−1)+10λ+8=02λ2+8λ+8=02(λ2+4λ+4)=0(λ+2)2=0.

Hence, we have a double root λ=−2. Therefore, the general solution is y(t)=c1t−2+c2t−2ln⁡t.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Cauchy-Euler Equation with a Repeated Root
content.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
2{t}^{2}{y}^{″}+10t{y}^{′}+8y=0,\,t>0.
$$
content.worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={t}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {t}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}+10t\cdot \lambda {t}^{\lambda -1}+8{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ 2\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }+10\lambda {t}^{\lambda }+8{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[2\lambda (\lambda -1)+10\lambda +8] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2\lambda (\lambda -1)+10\lambda +8 & =0 \\ 2{\lambda }^{2}+8\lambda +8 & =0 \\ 2({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +4) & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =-2.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(t)={c}_{1}{t}^{-2}+{c}_{2}{t}^{-2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.
$$

Question 6
?

Find the solution of the initial value problem x2y″−9xy′+25y=0,y(1)=−2,y′(1)=4,x>0.

a
y(x)=2x5(ln⁡x+1)
b
y(x)=2x5(ln⁡x+2)
c
y(x)=x−5(7ln⁡x−2)
d
y(x)=2x5(7ln⁡x−1)
e
y(x)=x−5(ln⁡x−1)
Submit

decision.explanation: The characteristic equation is r(r-1)-9r+25=(r-5)^2=0, so y=x^5(c₁+c₂ ln x). From y(1)=-2, c₁=-2. Since y′(1)=5c₁+c₂=4, c₂=14. Thus y=2x^5(7 ln x-1), matching option d.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Find the solution of the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-9x{y}^{′}+25y=0,\,y(1)=-2,\,{y}^{′}(1)=4,\,x>0.
$$
after.worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={x}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {x}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}-9x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+25{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }-9\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+25{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)-9\lambda +25] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)-9\lambda +25 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +25 & =0 \\ (\lambda -5)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =5.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(x)={c}_{1}{x}^{5}+{c}_{2}{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.
$$

Now let's find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$

Substituting $y(1)=-2$ into the general solution gives

$$
-2={c}_{1}.
$$

We now need to apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=4.$ First, we differentiate $y$ to find ${y}^{′}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =5{x}^{4}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}{x}^{4}+5{c}_{2}{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=4$ and ${c}_{1}=-2$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =5{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\ 4 & =-10+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =14.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(x) & =-2{x}^{5}+14{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =2{x}^{5}(7\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 6
?

Find the solution of the initial value problem x2y″−9xy′+25y=0,y(1)=−2,y′(1)=4,x>0.

a
y(x)=2x5(ln⁡x+1)
b
y(x)=2x5(ln⁡x+2)
c
y(x)=x−5(7ln⁡x−2)
d
y(x)=2x5(7ln⁡x−1)
e
y(x)=x−5(ln⁡x−1)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form y=xλ. Differentiating y with respect to x gives

y′=λxλ−1,y″=λ(λ−1)xλ−2.

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

x2⋅λ(λ−1)xλ−2−9x⋅λxλ−1+25xλ=0λ(λ−1)xλ−9λxλ+25xλ=0xλ[λ(λ−1)−9λ+25]=0.

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

λ(λ−1)−9λ+25=0λ2−10λ+25=0(λ−5)2=0.

Hence, we have a double root λ=5. Therefore, the general solution is y(x)=c1x5+c2x5ln⁡x.

Now let's find the constants c1 and c2.

Substituting y(1)=−2 into the general solution gives −2=c1.

We now need to apply the condition y′(1)=4. First, we differentiate y to find y′: y′=5x4c1+c2x4+5c2x4ln⁡x

Substituting y′(1)=4 and c1=−2 into the above gives 4=5c1+c24=−10+c2c2=14.

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is y(x)=−2x5+14x5ln⁡x=2x5(7ln⁡x−1).

verification.explanation: The characteristic equation is (r-5)^2=0, giving y=x^5(c₁+c₂ ln x). The initial conditions imply c₁=-2 and 5c₁+c₂=4, hence c₂=14. Therefore y=2x^5(7 ln x-1), confirming option d and the revealed solution.

content.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem Involving a Cauchy-Euler Equation with a Repeated Root
content.problem:
Find the solution of the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-9x{y}^{′}+25y=0,\,y(1)=-2,\,{y}^{′}(1)=4,\,x>0.
$$
content.worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={x}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {x}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}-9x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+25{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }-9\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+25{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)-9\lambda +25] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)-9\lambda +25 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +25 & =0 \\ (\lambda -5)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =5.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(x)={c}_{1}{x}^{5}+{c}_{2}{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.
$$

Now let's find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$

Substituting $y(1)=-2$ into the general solution gives

$$
-2={c}_{1}.
$$

We now need to apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=4.$ First, we differentiate $y$ to find ${y}^{′}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =5{x}^{4}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}{x}^{4}+5{c}_{2}{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=4$ and ${c}_{1}=-2$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =5{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\ 4 & =-10+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =14.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(x) & =-2{x}^{5}+14{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =2{x}^{5}(7\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

before.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-17t{y}^{′}+81y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={c}_{1}{t}^{9}+{c}_{2}{t}^{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡t,
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-17t{y}^{′}+81y,\,y(1)=0,\,{y}^{′}(1)=3,\,t>0.
$$

Question 7
?

Given that the differential equation

t2y″−17ty′+81y=0

has the general solution

y=c1t9+c2t9ln⁡t,

solve the initial value problem

t2y″−17ty′+81y,y(1)=0,y′(1)=3,t>0.

a
y(t)=4t9−3t9ln⁡t
b
y(t)=t9ln⁡t
c
y(t)=2t9+3t9ln⁡t
d
y(t)=−2t9ln⁡t
e
y(t)=3t9ln⁡t
Submit

decision.explanation: The characteristic equation is r(r-1)-17r+81=(r-9)^2=0. Using y=t^9(c₁+c₂ ln t), y(1)=0 gives c₁=0, and y′(1)=9c₁+c₂=3 gives c₂=3. Thus option e satisfies the differential equation and both initial conditions.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-17t{y}^{′}+81y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={c}_{1}{t}^{9}+{c}_{2}{t}^{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡t,
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-17t{y}^{′}+81y,\,y(1)=0,\,{y}^{′}(1)=3,\,t>0.
$$
after.worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- First, we apply the condition $y(1)=0.$ Substituting $y(1)=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
0={c}_{1}.
$$

- Then, we apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=3.$ Differentiating $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =9{c}_{1}{t}^{8}+{c}_{2}{t}^{8}+9{c}_{2}{t}^{8}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=3$ and ${c}_{1}=0$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =9{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\ 3 & =0+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(t) & =3{t}^{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Given that the differential equation

t2y″−17ty′+81y=0

has the general solution

y=c1t9+c2t9ln⁡t,

solve the initial value problem

t2y″−17ty′+81y,y(1)=0,y′(1)=3,t>0.

a
y(t)=4t9−3t9ln⁡t
b
y(t)=t9ln⁡t
c
y(t)=2t9+3t9ln⁡t
d
y(t)=−2t9ln⁡t
e
y(t)=3t9ln⁡t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We find the constants c1 and c2 using the initial conditions.

  • First, we apply the condition y(1)=0. Substituting y(1)=0 into the general solution gives 0=c1.

  • Then, we apply the condition y′(1)=3. Differentiating y, we get y′=9c1t8+c2t8+9c2t8ln⁡t.

Substituting y′(1)=3 and c1=0 into the above gives 3=9c1+c23=0+c2c2=3.

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is y(t)=3t9ln⁡t.

content.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-17t{y}^{′}+81y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={c}_{1}{t}^{9}+{c}_{2}{t}^{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡t,
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-17t{y}^{′}+81y,\,y(1)=0,\,{y}^{′}(1)=3,\,t>0.
$$
content.worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- First, we apply the condition $y(1)=0.$ Substituting $y(1)=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
0={c}_{1}.
$$

- Then, we apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=3.$ Differentiating $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =9{c}_{1}{t}^{8}+{c}_{2}{t}^{8}+9{c}_{2}{t}^{8}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=3$ and ${c}_{1}=0$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =9{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\ 3 & =0+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(t) & =3{t}^{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Given that the differential equation

x2y″+15xy′+49y=0

has the general solution

y=c1x−7+c2x−7ln⁡x,

solve the initial value problem

x2y″+15xy′+49y=0,y(1)=1,y′(1)=1,x>0.

a
y(x)=2−8ln⁡xx7
b
 y(x)=1−6ln⁡xx7
c
y(x)=1+8ln⁡xx7
d
 y(x)=2−12ln⁡xx7
e
 y(x)=1+6ln⁡xx7
Submit

decision.explanation: Using y=x⁻⁷(c₁+c₂ ln x), the condition y(1)=1 gives c₁=1. Differentiating gives y′(1)=-7c₁+c₂=1, so c₂=8. Thus y=(1+8 ln x)/x⁷, matching option c.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+15x{y}^{′}+49y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={c}_{1}{x}^{-7}+{c}_{2}{x}^{-7}\operatorname{ln}⁡x,
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+15x{y}^{′}+49y=0,\,y(1)=1,\,{y}^{′}(1)=1,\,x>0.
$$
after.worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- First, we apply the condition $y(1)=1.$ Substituting $y(1)=1$ into the general solution gives

$$
1={c}_{1}.
$$

- Then, we apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=1.$ Differentiating $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =-7{c}_{1}{x}^{-8}+{c}_{2}{x}^{-8}-7{c}_{2}{x}^{-8}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=1$ and ${c}_{1}=1$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =-7(1)+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(x) & ={x}^{-7}+8{x}^{-7}\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =\frac{1+8\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{7}}.\end{aligned}

after.html:
Question 8
?

Given that the differential equation

x2y″+15xy′+49y=0

has the general solution

y=c1x−7+c2x−7ln⁡x,

solve the initial value problem

x2y″+15xy′+49y=0,y(1)=1,y′(1)=1,x>0.

a
y(x)=2−8ln⁡xx7
b
 y(x)=1−6ln⁡xx7
c
y(x)=1+8ln⁡xx7
d
 y(x)=2−12ln⁡xx7
e
 y(x)=1+6ln⁡xx7
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We find the constants c1 and c2 using the initial conditions.

  • First, we apply the condition y(1)=1. Substituting y(1)=1 into the general solution gives 1=c1.

  • Then, we apply the condition y′(1)=1. Differentiating y, we get y′=−7c1x−8+c2x−8−7c2x−8ln⁡x.

Substituting y′(1)=1 and c1=1 into the above gives 1=−7(1)+c2c2=8.

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is y(x)=x−7+8x−7ln⁡x=1+8ln⁡xx7.

verification.explanation: The characteristic equation is (r+7)^2=0. In y=x⁻⁷(c₁+c₂ ln x), y(1)=1 gives c₁=1, and y′(1)=-7c₁+c₂=1 gives c₂=8. Thus option c matches the initial conditions and the revealed worked solution.

content.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem Involving a Cauchy-Euler Equation with a Repeated Root
content.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+15x{y}^{′}+49y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={c}_{1}{x}^{-7}+{c}_{2}{x}^{-7}\operatorname{ln}⁡x,
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+15x{y}^{′}+49y=0,\,y(1)=1,\,{y}^{′}(1)=1,\,x>0.
$$
content.worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- First, we apply the condition $y(1)=1.$ Substituting $y(1)=1$ into the general solution gives

$$
1={c}_{1}.
$$

- Then, we apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=1.$ Differentiating $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =-7{c}_{1}{x}^{-8}+{c}_{2}{x}^{-8}-7{c}_{2}{x}^{-8}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=1$ and ${c}_{1}=1$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =-7(1)+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(x) & ={x}^{-7}+8{x}^{-7}\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =\frac{1+8\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{7}}.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 9
?

Given that the differential equation

x2y″−xy′+y=0

has the general solution

y=c1x+c2xln⁡x,

solve the initial value problem

x2y″−xy′+y=0,y(1)=1,y′(1)=4,x>0.

a
y(x)=2x−5xln⁡x
b
y(x)=x+3xln⁡x
c
y(x)=x−xln⁡x
d
y(x)=x2−2xln⁡x
e
y(x)=x−4xln⁡x
Submit

decision.explanation: From y=c₁x+c₂x ln x, y(1)=1 gives c₁=1. Differentiating gives y′=c₁+c₂(ln x+1), so y′(1)=1+c₂=4 implies c₂=3. Therefore y=x+3x ln x, matching option b.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-x{y}^{′}+y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={c}_{1}x+{c}_{2}x\operatorname{ln}⁡x,
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-x{y}^{′}+y=0,\,y(1)=1,\,{y}^{′}(1)=4,\,x>0.
$$
after.worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- First, we apply the condition $y(1)=1.$ Substituting $y(1)=1$ into the general solution gives

$$
1={c}_{1}.
$$

- Then, we apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=1.$ Differentiating $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={c}_{1}+{c}_{2}+{c}_{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=1$ and ${c}_{1}=1$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =1+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(x)=x+3x\operatorname{ln}⁡x.
$$

Question 10
?

Given that the differential equation

x2y″−7xy′+16y=0

has the general solution

y=c1x4+c2x4ln⁡x,

solve the initial value problem

x2y″−7xy′+16y=0,y(1)=2,y′(1)=6,x>0.

a
y(x)=2x4−x4ln⁡x
b
y(x)=−2x4+3x4ln⁡x
c
y(x)=2x4−3x4ln⁡x
d
y(x)=2x4−2x4ln⁡x
e
y(x)=−3x4−4x4ln⁡x
Submit

decision.explanation: From y=x⁴(c₁+c₂ ln x), y(1)=2 gives c₁=2. Differentiating yields y′(1)=4c₁+c₂=6, so c₂=-2. Therefore y=2x⁴-2x⁴ ln x, matching option d.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-7x{y}^{′}+16y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={c}_{1}{x}^{4}+{c}_{2}{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x,
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-7x{y}^{′}+16y=0,\,y(1)=2,\,{y}^{′}(1)=6,\,x>0.
$$
after.worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- First, we apply the condition $y(1)=2.$ Substituting $y(1)=2$ into the general solution gives

$$
2={c}_{1}.
$$

- Then, we apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=6.$ Differentiating $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =4{c}_{1}{x}^{3}+{c}_{2}{x}^{3}+4{c}_{2}{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=6$ and ${c}_{1}=2$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =4(2)+{c}_{2} \\ 6 & =8+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(x)=2{x}^{4}-2{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.
$$

Question 10
?

Given that the differential equation

x2y″−7xy′+16y=0

has the general solution

y=c1x4+c2x4ln⁡x,

solve the initial value problem

x2y″−7xy′+16y=0,y(1)=2,y′(1)=6,x>0.

a
y(x)=2x4−x4ln⁡x
b
y(x)=−2x4+3x4ln⁡x
c
y(x)=2x4−3x4ln⁡x
d
y(x)=2x4−2x4ln⁡x
e
y(x)=−3x4−4x4ln⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We find the constants c1 and c2 using the initial conditions.

  • First, we apply the condition y(1)=2. Substituting y(1)=2 into the general solution gives 2=c1.

  • Then, we apply the condition y′(1)=6. Differentiating y, we get y′=4c1x3+c2x3+4c2x3ln⁡x.

Substituting y′(1)=6 and c1=2 into the above gives 6=4(2)+c26=8+c2c2=−2.

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is y(x)=2x4−2x4ln⁡x.

content.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem Involving a Cauchy-Euler Equation with a Repeated Root
content.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-7x{y}^{′}+16y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={c}_{1}{x}^{4}+{c}_{2}{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x,
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-7x{y}^{′}+16y=0,\,y(1)=2,\,{y}^{′}(1)=6,\,x>0.
$$
content.worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- First, we apply the condition $y(1)=2.$ Substituting $y(1)=2$ into the general solution gives

$$
2={c}_{1}.
$$

- Then, we apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=6.$ Differentiating $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =4{c}_{1}{x}^{3}+{c}_{2}{x}^{3}+4{c}_{2}{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=6$ and ${c}_{1}=2$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =4(2)+{c}_{2} \\ 6 & =8+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(x)=2{x}^{4}-2{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.
$$
